decisions.rationale: ONT-CONTEXT: The operator explicitly requires all project specifications to use verified ontology vocabulary. The Project selection and Terminology coverage sections propose the context model; no selector, canonical schema or enforcement is implemented.

ONT-INPUTS: The Project selection and immutable inputs section extends the existing single-package snapshot concept to a proposed checked context and dependency closure. Existing snapshot code is only inspected context; no runtime consumer or dependency resolver changes in this PR.

ONT-COVERAGE: The Terminology coverage section requires scoped source-located assessment and keeps unassessed prose explicit. The full coverage profile and semantic reviewer are future work; this text is not a successful assessment of the current corpus.

ONT-GAPS: The operator permits structurally valid ontologies with gaps. The action-specific table retains usable resolved vocabulary while withholding full grounding for required unresolved terms; no new gate or term acceptance is activated.

ONT-DRAFT: The operator endorsed preserving conversational capture before terminology resolution. The readiness table proposes the boundary between drafts and dependent actions; current capture code and canonical permissions are unchanged.

ONT-FRESHNESS: The Freshness, reuse and Supervisor section proposes binding all influencing context/spec/binding/policy inputs rather than trusting artifact presence. No cache admission, freshness implementation or Supervisor decision code is introduced.

ONT-MIGRATION: The migration rows and delivery sequence propose preserving IDs/history and making unassessed legacy scope and exceptions visible. No canonical vocabulary assignment, historical revision rewrite or approved exception is produced.

ONT-VIEW: The SpecSpace section reuses inspected workspace endpoints and preserves browser-local /ontology exploration. No SpecSpace endpoint, UI parser, trust badge or project-selection behavior changes here.

ONT-TRUST: The responsibility table and scoped review rules distinguish formal checking, terminology review, human acceptance and future intent preservation. This contract-only design grants no model/compiler approval authority and introduces no production decision.
